services.title: A solid foundation.
services.label: 01 / DESIGN & BUILD

steps.title: First, a conversation.
steps.text: We discuss your workloads, current environment, and goals to see whether a private platform fits.

steps.title: Assess. Then scope.
steps.text: A paid assessment turns hardware, network, and workload requirements into an architecture, risk review, and fixed-price proposal.

steps.title: Build it. Prove it.
steps.text: We deliver the agreed platform, validate its operation, and test recovery within the scope of your package.

steps.title: Make it yours.
steps.text: Architecture diagrams, operating and recovery runbooks, and scoped handoff sessions give your team a practical path to ownership.

steps.title: Keep it in good shape.
steps.text: Choose handoff only, advisory or scheduled platform care. A qualified client operator or MSP owns operations and incident response.

faqs.q: What do we have at the end?
faqs.a: The deliverables agreed in your proposal, with documentation and a practical handoff. Production launches include delivery, secure access, monitoring, applicable tested recovery and a defined stabilization period. Ongoing support is optional with a qualified operator.

You purchase and own the hardware, accounts, licenses, warranties, and replacement parts. We specify requirements and review compatibility. Hardware, internet, DNS, third-party services, shipping, travel, and applicable taxes are excluded unless the proposal includes them.

A free discovery call establishes fit. A small-workload assessment is $1,500–$2,500; broader production assessment is $3,000–$4,000. Pilot and launch fees exclude assessment unless expressly bundled. Written scope defines acceptance criteria and implementation fees. A 50% scheduling deposit and remaining milestone payments are agreed in the proposal.

faqs.q: What does ongoing platform care include?
faqs.a: Support is optional with a qualified operator, with no default annual commitment. Advisory is $500–$750 per month for scheduled review and 1–2 hours of advice. Scheduled Platform Care starts at $1,500 per month for agreed maintenance of one named environment within written capacity limits. Best-effort response within two business days for routine covered requests; no 24/7 coverage or guaranteed restoration. Your operator or MSP owns incident response.

faqs.q: Can our legacy virtual machines move into the cluster?
faqs.a: Potentially. A KubeVirt / legacy-VM assessment starts at $5,000 and reviews dependencies, hardware compatibility, networking, storage, licensing, and recovery. We pilot an agreed workload, then plan staged migration with rollback, validation, documentation, and training. Implementation is quoted separately. Compatibility and zero-downtime migration are not guaranteed.

faqs.q: Can we run GPUs and private AI workflows?
faqs.a: Yes, as separately scoped options. GPU enablement starts at $15,000 and private AI workflow enablement at $10,000. We first check hardware, workloads, access, storage, and operational requirements. Hardware and model or service licenses are separate; custom AI application development requires its own scope.

faqs.q: Can you work with an existing platform or IT provider?
faqs.a: We can assess an existing Kubernetes environment and scope improvements, integrations, or migration. We work alongside internal teams and IT providers. Application defects, developer workflow support, legacy application support, and unapproved changes are outside platform care unless explicitly contracted.

faqs.q: Can you work remotely or on site?
faqs.a: Both can be scoped after reviewing your environment and access requirements. On-site installation, travel, and shipping are priced separately. Any equipment staging or provisioning before shipment is agreed in the proposal.
